audit.title: Get a Random Number
audit.summary: This is a solid, complete step-by-step tutorial for requesting VRF v2.5 randomness via the direct-funding (Wrapper) method, with a full runnable contract and concrete on-chain values. Its biggest GEO strength is code completeness and concrete specifics (hardcoded Sepolia addresses, gas limits, real cost figures). Its biggest opportunity is discoverability and prior-resistance: the page carries no verifiable structured metadata (0 JSON-LD blocks, missing canonical, no dates) and no symptom-phrased headings, so retrieval and self-standing extractability lag the content quality. Honest verdict: good, agent-usable content whose retrievability and answer-first framing are underbuilt relative to the doc's technical strength.

recommendations.title: Add structured metadata (TechArticle JSON-LD + canonical + dates)
recommendations.change: emit a `TechArticle` JSON-LD block with `headline`, `dateModified`, `programmingLanguage: Solidity`, and a `<link rel="canonical">`; surface a visible "Last updated" line.
recommendations.why: freshness and schema are trust/parse signals engines use to rank and cite; their absence is a verified gap.

recommendations.title: Add symptom/error-phrased troubleshooting section
recommendations.issue: no error-string headings; devs query "VRF request not fulfilled" / "request not found"
recommendations.change: add "Troubleshooting" with H3s like *"My requestRandomWords transaction succeeds but no random words return"*, *"Error: request not found"*, *"Callback fails / out of gas"*, each answered in the first sentence.
recommendations.why: symptom-phrased headings win retrieval that concept-titled prose loses.

recommendations.title: Lead each section with a self-contained answer
recommendations.issue: sections open with "Return to Remix..." / procedural context
recommendations.change: prepend a one-sentence canonical statement, e.g. "Call `requestRandomWords(bool enableNativePayment)` to request randomness; VRF returns values via the `fulfillRandomWords()` callback within a few minutes."
recommendations.why: a lifted chunk must stand alone to be quoted.

recommendations.title: Add a canonical definition of VRF v2.5 direct funding
recommendations.issue: no crisp liftable definition near first use
recommendations.change: add: "Direct funding is a VRF v2.5 payment method where the consuming contract pays per request in LINK or native tokens at request time, with no subscription to manage."
recommendations.why: gives engines a verbatim answer to "what is VRF direct funding."

recommendations.title: Convert request-parameter list to a table
recommendations.issue: parameters `callbackGasLimit`/`requestConfirmations`/`numWords` explained in prose bullets; 0 tables on page
recommendations.change: add a table with columns Parameter | Type | Default | Constraint | Notes.
recommendations.why: tables let engines extract reasons and defaults cleanly and split the oversized section.

recommendations.title: Name direct funding vs subscription explicitly to resist prior substitution
recommendations.issue: engines may default to the subscription method (the more common VRF idiom)
recommendations.change: add one line: "This page uses direct funding (`VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase`). If you want a shared subscription instead, use the subscription guide — do not mix the two base contracts."
recommendations.why: explicitly names the tempting-wrong alternative as a Don't.

antiPatterns: Vague quantifiers ("many, several") in parameter descriptions — minor; replace with figures where possible.
One section (797 words) exceeds the 600-word chunk boundary; splitting via the parameter table above resolves it.
No stale-date risk visible, but also no date at all — undated content is a trust gap.
offPageNotes: `llms.txt` is already linked from the page — good; ensure this URL is enumerated in it.
Site-level JSON-LD/canonical templating likely governs the missing metadata; fix at the template layer, not per page.
Freshness cadence: publish and surface `dateModified` sitewide so engines can prefer current VRF v2.5 content over older v2 pages.
